title: Testimony Without Decades
script: Rina: [thoughtful] Bagas, something's always puzzled me about Abu Hurairah. He only knew the Prophet for a few years, yet he's credited with more transmitted hadith than companions who knew him for decades.
Bagas: That discrepancy bothered skeptics too, both then and now. The explanation, though, has less to do with proximity and more with circumstance.
Rina: [carefully] What circumstance made him so unusually prolific?
Bagas: He had no household or trade competing for his attention, unlike companions managing farms, families, or commerce, so he spent his days essentially attached to the Prophet's presence.
Rina: [reflective] So volume reflects available time rather than any implied favoritism or exaggeration?
Bagas: Largely, yes, though he also developed what amounts to a discipline of memorization, requesting the Prophet's prayer that his retention never fade.
Rina: [honestly] He actually asked for that specifically?
Bagas: Reportedly, yes, spreading his cloak during a lesson and asking the Prophet to gather his words into it, metaphorically, so nothing would be forgotten.
Rina: [gently] Did his contemporaries ever challenge the accuracy of what he transmitted, given how much material he alone produced?
Bagas: Occasionally, and rigorously, actually. Later scholars cross-examined his narrations against other transmitters with considerable scrutiny, precisely because volume alone invites suspicion.
Rina: [calmly] And how did his material hold up under that scrutiny?
Bagas: Remarkably well, on the whole. Discrepancies existed, as they do with any transmitter, but nothing suggesting systematic distortion or embellishment.
Rina: [encouraging] It's an interesting epistemic problem, isn't it, verifying testimony generations after the fact, without any of the usual physical evidence.
Bagas: Exactly, which is why the scholarly tradition built around hadith verification remains genuinely impressive, treating memory as something that requires the same rigor as any other evidence.
Rina: [seriously] So his legacy isn't really about sheer output, it's about how thoroughly that output withstood examination.
Bagas: Precisely. Quantity would mean very little without the verification apparatus built specifically to interrogate it.

quiz.question: Why was Abu Hurairah able to transmit so much hadith despite knowing the Prophet only a few years?
options: He had no household or trade competing for his attention, so he stayed near the Prophet constantly
He had a photographic ability from birth
